title: Part in Peace! Is Day Before Us
description: Part in Peace! Is Day Before Us in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Sarah Flower Adams wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 60, “Peace be with You”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Part in peace! is day be-fore us? Praise His name for life and light; Are the sha-dows length-ening o'er us? Bless His care who guards the night.

lines: Part in peace! is day before us?
Praise His name for life and light;
Are the shadows lengthening o'er us?
Bless His care who guards the night.
Part in peace! with deep thanksgiving,
Part in peace! such are the praises

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Sarah Flower Adams died in 1848.
credits: Words by Sarah Flower Adams (1805–1848), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
